Subject: Jarvis connector - MSA / DPA / SOW redlines and procurement path

Hi Amy / Jarvis team,

Thanks again for the productive call last week — excited by the product fit and the joint GTM potential. Attached are our proposed redlines to the MSA and a short SOW template that maps the integration milestones we discussed. Key asks up front:

- Narrow the indemnity to product-related claims only (we flagged specific language in the MSA).
- Limit data processing scope to token-level inference metadata; preserve customer data residency commitments in the DPA.
- Clarify acceptance criteria and timelines in the SOW — we added an explicit rollback trigger for non-functional regression during canary.

We'd like to close the legal loop this week so Procurement can issue a PO and engineering can schedule the integration sprint. Rafael (copied) will lead commercial alignment; Karthik will review any legal counterpoints.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redlines_20260803.pdf (redline), Redwood_SOW_template_20260803.docx

Proposed next steps:
1) Jarvis legal returns counter-redlines by EOD Wed 8/5
2) We triage any material issues and aim for an exec signoff call Thurs 8/6
3) Procurement to issue PO upon signoff

Thanks — looking forward to moving fast.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Redwood Inference — "Predictable inference at scale"

From: Amy Liu <amy.liu@jarvis.ai>

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jarvis connector - MSA / DPA / SOW redlines and procurement path

Vanessa — thanks for the redlines and the clear steps. We reviewed internally and have a few counterpoints attached. High level:

- Indemnity: we can accept limiting to product-related claims but need a reciprocal carve for third-party IP where Jarvis provides connectors or prebuilt adapters.
- Data scope: Jarvis requires a limited right to log inference metadata for telemetry (30 days) — hoping we can align the retention with your observability needs.
- SOW: dates look fine; one ask is to move the acceptance window from 14 days to 21 days to allow enterprise QA.

Attached: Jarvis_MSA_counter_20260803.pdf (redline), Jarvis_SOW_draft_20260803.docx

We can do a short 30-min call tomorrow to go through the top 3 items. If that works, Brian can set up.

Best,
Amy Liu
Head of Legal Operations, Jarvis AI
amy.liu@jarvis.ai

Subject: Fwd: Jarvis counterpoints (quick internal alignment)

Folks — forwarding Jarvis' counter-redlines. Quick thoughts below before I respond:

- Indemnity: reciprocal third-party IP carve seems reasonable but we should not accept broad customer IP indemnities tied to Jarvis connectors. Recommend: accept their carve but limit aggregate exposure to the contract value and exclude willful misconduct.
- Telemetry retention: 30 days for aggregated telemetry is OK if we add strict PII carveouts + attestations in the DPA.
- Acceptance window: 21 days is acceptable for their QA, but add a staged acceptance (canary acceptance at 7 days, full acceptance at 21).

Rafael — any commercial constraints with the PO timing if we accept the IP carve?
Karthik — can you draft two short paragraphs to propose back to Jarvis on indemnity + telemetry? I'll handle the acceptance cadence language.

Thanks — V.

Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Jarvis counterpoints (quick internal alignment)

Vanessa, Rafael — draft language below you can send to Jarvis. Keep it tight so legal seats can review quickly:

1) Indemnity (proposed reply): "Each party shall indemnify the other for third-party claims arising from the indemnifying party's breach, its gross negligence or willful misconduct. For claims related to third-party IP, each party's liability shall be capped at the total fees paid under this Agreement in the prior 12 months; neither party will be liable for indirect or consequential damages. Jarvis-provided connectors must be specifically identified and limited to the functionality described in the SOW."

2) Telemetry / data retention (proposed reply): "Jarvis may retain aggregated inference telemetry and anonymized logs for 30 days strictly for reliability and product analytics. Any telemetry containing customer-identifiable data must be hashed and redacted; retention beyond 30 days requires written consent and must be documented in the DPA annex."

I also suggest we propose the staged acceptance: 7-day canary acceptance (limited traffic), followed by a 21-day full acceptance window. If no material defects are reported in the canary, the SOW moves to full acceptance.

If that looks good I can convert to redline comments; otherwise let me know edits.

— Karthik
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Jarvis connector - MSA / DPA / SOW redlines and procurement path

Amy / Brian — thanks for the quick turnaround and the SOW draft. We had an internal pass and are proposing the following compromise (see brief bullets below; updated redlines attached):

- Indemnity: we can accept a reciprocal IP carve limited to the Jarvis connectors described in the SOW; liability cap tied to 12 months fees and exclusion of indirect damages. We will not accept language tying Redwood to Jarvis' customer IP claims beyond connector scope.
- Telemetry: Jarvis may retain aggregated telemetry for 30 days for reliability/analytics; any data with customer-identifiable elements must be hashed/removed and cannot be used for model training.
- Acceptance cadence: propose 7-day canary acceptance (low traffic), then 21-day full acceptance. Non-functional regressions that fail performance SLOs during canary trigger a rollback clause in the SOW.

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_redlines_20260804.pdf (updated with Karthik's language), Redwood_SOW_final_20260804.docx

If you're aligned we can schedule an executive signoff call Thur 8/6 at 10am PT. Rafael — will Procurement be able to issue a PO immediately after signoff?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
